newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINE BONDS END UP, CONFIDENCE RETURNING.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINE BONDS END UP, CONFIDENCE RETURNING.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher Wednesday as the market continued to recover confidence after the declines at the end of last week, with traders predicting gains could pick up momentum in coming sessions.
"The market was very firm. Everything is returning to normal," said a trader at a local bank, pointing to the bullish tone that has dominated most of this year.
Argentina's Par Brady bond was up 1/4 at 74-7/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was up $0.35 at 119.90.
Traders said the market was helped by the release of Argentine central government deficit figures showing a July shortfall of $198.6 million, sharply down from $788.7 the same month a year earlier.
"The deficit figures were very good," said another trader.
Players said the market was also beginning to favorably digest the news of the center-left alliance between the Frepaso coalition and the Radical Party this week.
"The alliance was well received by investors because it shows the democratic system is maturing," said the first trader.
"There is a feeling that it will lead to an attack on issues like corruption and unemployment which have been missing."
In the money market, three month peso BAIBOR, or Buenos Aires interbank offered rate, rose to 7.1875 percent from 7.1250 percent.
